title: The Quran Names a Steep Climb, Then Tells You What Is on It
excerpt: Surah Al-Balad opens with a man boasting about how much he has spent, then names a steep pass he never attempted — and stops to define it. The definition runs four lines, built almost entirely from words the Quran uses nowhere else, and every item on it is a transfer of wealth.
seo_title: Al-'Aqabah in Surah Al-Balad: The Steep Climb Is Freeing and Feeding (90:11–16)
seo_description: Al-Balad defines its own image: the steep pass is freeing a neck, feeding on a day of hunger, an orphan, a poor man in the dust. Built from hapax vocabulary — masghabah, matrabah, najdayn, marḥamah.
